sanskrit: yau hemantaṃ svāpayatho balena- -arvāg devebhya uta yau paro divaḥ | bhavārudrayoḥ sumatiṃ vṛṇīmahe 'nyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: You two who lull winter to sleep by your power — you who dwell this side of the gods and you who dwell beyond the sky — we choose the benevolence of Bhava and Rudra; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: yo dyām ātanoti yo 'ntarikṣaṃ stabhnāty ojaso jāyamānaḥ | tasmai rudrāya haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: He who stretches out the sky, who props up the atmosphere, being born of vital force — to that Rudra we would render homage with oblation; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: yayor vadhān nāpapadyate kiṃ cana- -antar deveṣūta mānuṣeṣu | tābhyāṃ rudrābhyāṃ haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: From whose deadly stroke nothing escapes, among the gods or among human beings — to those two Rudras we would render homage with oblation; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: yāv īśāte paśūnāṃ pārthivānāṃ catuṣpadām uta vā ye dvipādaḥ | tābhyāṃ rudrābhyāṃ haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: You two who are lords of the earthly animals — of the four-footed and of those that are two-footed — to those two Rudras we would render homage with oblation; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: yasya pratihitāyāḥ saṃ viśanta āraṇyāḥ paśava uta grāmyāsaḥ | tasmai rudrāya haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: Into whose quiver the wild beasts and the tame cattle enter together — to that Rudra we would render homage with oblation; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: yasmād oṣadhayo barbhriyamāṇā yanti yasmād vṛkṣāso na viyanti viśve | vayāṃsi yasmāt pracaranti bhīṣā tasmai rudrāya haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: From whom the trembling herbs take flight, from whom all the trees do not stray, from whom the birds move abroad in fear — to that Rudra we would render homage with oblation; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: yaḥ parvatān vidadhe 'ti vidvān yo bhūtāni kalpayati prajānan | tasmai rudrāya haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: He who set the mountains in place, supremely knowing, who ordains all beings with full awareness — to that Rudra we would render homage with oblation; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: yāv īśānau carato dvipado 'sya catuṣpadaḥ | yā ugrau kṣipradhanvānau tābhyāṃ rudrābhyāṃ haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: You two who, as sovereigns, roam over his two-footed and four-footed creatures, you two who are fierce and swift of bow — to those two Rudras we would render homage with oblation; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: punaś cakṣuḥ punaḥ prāṇaṃ punar āyur dhehi no jātavedaḥ | rudra jalāṣabheṣaja vidvāṃsas ta enā haviṣā vidhema- -anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā vy etu ||
english: Restore to us sight, restore breath, restore life, O Jātavedas; O Rudra, healer with cooling balm — knowing this, with this oblation we render homage to you; let the deadly poison go elsewhere from us.

sanskrit: īśānaṃ tvā bheṣajānāṃ vijeṣāya vṛṇīmahe | cakre sahasravīryaṃ sarasvān oṣadhe tvā ||
english: We choose you, the lord of healing herbs, for the sake of conquest; Sarasvān has made you, O herb, of a thousand potencies.

sanskrit: satyajitaṃ śapathayāvanīṃ sahamānāṃ punaḥsarām | sarvāḥ sam ahvy oṣadhīr ito mā pārayān iti ||
english: The truly victorious one, the driver-away of curses, the overpowering one, the one that returns — I have summoned all the herbs together, saying: 'Let her carry away from here.'

sanskrit: yā śaśāpa śapanena yā vā gha mūram ādadhe | yā vā rasasya prāśāya- -ārebhe tokam attu sā ||
english: She who has cursed with a curse, or who has grasped at utter folly, or who has undertaken to steal the sap — let her devour her own offspring.

sanskrit: pratīcīnaphalo hi tvam apāmārga babhūvitha | sarvān mac chapathām̐ adhi varīyo yāvayā tvam ||
english: For you, O Apāmārga, came to be with fruit turned backward; drive away from me all curses more broadly than all others.

sanskrit: yac ca bhrātṛvyaḥ śapati yac ca jāmiḥ śapāti naḥ | brahmā yan manyutaḥ śapāt sarvaṃ tan no adhaspadam ||
english: That which a rival curses, and that which a kinsman curses upon us, and that which the brahmin curses out of anger — let all of that be beneath our feet.

sanskrit: yāṃ te cakrur āme pātre yāṃ sūtre nīlalohite | āme māṃse kṛtyāṃ yāṃ cakrus tayā kṛtyākṛto jahi ||
english: The sorcery they have made for you in a raw vessel, in a blue-red thread, the sorcery they have made in raw flesh — with that very sorcery slay the sorcerer.

sanskrit: duṣvapnyaṃ durjīvitaṃ rakṣo abhvam arāyyaḥ | durvācaḥ sarvaṃ durbhūtaṃ tad ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Ill omen from bad dreams, wretched existence, the demon, the monstrous, the niggards, evil speech, all evil being — all that we drive away from here.

sanskrit: kṣudhāmāraṃ tṛṣṇāmāram agotām anapatyatām | apāmārga tvayā vayaṃ sarvaṃ tad apa mṛjmahe ||
english: Death by hunger, death by thirst, lack of cattle, lack of offspring — with you, O Apāmārga, we wipe away all that.

sanskrit: samā bhūmiḥ sūryeṇa- -ahnā rātrī samāvatī | kṛṇomi satyam ūtaye arasāḥ santu kṛtvarīḥ ||
english: Even is the earth with the sun; night is equally provided with the day. I make this true formula for protection: let the sorceries be without power.

sanskrit: yo devāḥ kṛtyāṃ kṛtvā harād aviduṣo gṛham | vatso dhārur iva mātaraṃ taṃ pratyag upa padyatām ||
english: He, O gods, who makes sorcery and carries it into the house of one who is unaware — let it return upon him as a suckling calf returns to its mother.

sanskrit: amā kṛtvā pāpmānaṃ yas tayānyaṃ jighāṃsati | aśmānas tasyāṃ dagdhāyāṃ bahulāḥ phaṭ karikratu ||
english: He who makes the evil thing at home and with it seeks to slay another — when it is burned, may the many stones crack loudly against him.

sanskrit: sahasradhāman viśikhān vigrīvāñ chāyayā tvam | prati sma cakruṣe kṛtyāṃ priyāṃ priyāvate hara ||
english: O you of a thousand abodes, with bared arrows and twisted neck, with your shadow — carry back the beloved sorcery to the one who made it, to him who holds it dear.

sanskrit: yā cakāra na śaśāka śaśre pādam aṅgulim | cakāra bhadram asmabhyam abhagā bhagavadbhyaḥ ||
english: She who made it could not prevail; she has cut off her own foot, her finger; the unfortunate one has brought good fortune to us who are fortunate.

sanskrit: anayāham oṣadhyā sarvāḥ kṛtyā adūṣayam | yāṃ kṣetre cakrur yāṃ gobhyo yāṃ vā te puruṣebhyaḥ ||
english: With this herb I have rendered powerless all the sorceries — that which they made in the field, that which they made against the cattle, or that which they made against those men.

sanskrit: apāmārgo 'pa mārṣṭu kṣetriyaṃ śapathāṃś ca mat | apāha yātudhānyo 'pa sarvā arāyyaḥ ||
english: Let Apāmārga wipe away hereditary disease and curses from me; drive away the sorcerers, drive away all the niggards.

sanskrit: apamṛjya yātudhānān apa sarvā arāyyaḥ | apāmārga prajayā tvaṃ rayyā sacasva naḥ ||
english: Having wiped away the sorcerers, having wiped away all the niggards — O Apāmārga, accompany us with offspring and with wealth.
